answer: The strongest lever is simple: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because ridge only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, reef is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any summit approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
